source_refs.note: Exercise 11.1, Question 8: book page 290 (Q1-Q8). The book prints no answers for Unit 11; every answer here is ours.

blocks.prompt: 8 (i) Determine whether the following function is a scalar function or a vector-valued function. Give appropriate reasoning to support the answer: \(f(t) = (3t^2 - 5)^2\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh pehchanne (classification) ka sawal hai: faisla output ki qism se hota hai.
Har \(t\) ke liye yeh rule sirf ek number deta hai, is liye hum scalar function ki tawaqqo karte hain.
Rule: 11.3.1 ke criteria: ek number to scalar, kai components to vector.
Plan: \(t\) ki values rakh kar output dekhenge aur criteria se milayenge.
Yaad rakhein: faisla function ki shakal se nahin, output se hota hai.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(t) = (3t^2 - 5)^2\).
Maloom karna: yeh scalar hai ya vector-valued, aur kyun?
Tareeqa: 11.3.1 ke criteria: scalar function ka output ek akela number hota hai; vector-valued function ka output ordered tuple (components, ya \(\hat{i}, \hat{j}, \hat{k}\) ka combination) hota hai. \(t\) ki ek value rakh kar output dekhein.

\(t\) ki values rakhein
\[f(1) = (3 - 5)^2 = 4\]
\[f(0) = (-5)^2 = 25\]
Kyun: har input par sirf ek real number aata hai. Na koi components hain, na direction. Jaise thermometer sirf ek reading deta hai.
Dhyan dein: bahar wala square poore bracket ka hai: pehle \(3t^2 - 5\), phir us ka square.

Criteria lagayein
Output ek akela number: haan. Naam chhota italic \(f\), jaise kitab scalar functions ke liye istemal karti hai (11.3.1 (ii)).
Kyun: scalar function ka criterion (i) poora hota hai. Square ho, bracket ho, ya koi bhi algebra ho, aakhir mein jawab ek hi number hai.
Misaal: thermometer ki reading, kisi cheez ka wazan, ya potential energy: yeh sab scalar hain kyunke in mein direction nahin.

Tasdeeq
\(f(t)\) ek real number ka square hai, is liye har \(t \in \mathbb{R}\) par \(f(t) \ge 0\): yeh numbers ka set hai, vectors ka nahin \(\checkmark\).
blocks.final_answer: Scalar function: har input \(t\) par ek akela real number milta hai (misaal \(f(1) = 4\)); yahan har \(t \in \mathbb{R}\) par \(f(t) \ge 0\).

blocks.prompt: 8 (ii) Determine whether the following function is a scalar function or a vector-valued function. Give appropriate reasoning to support the answer: \(\mathbf{h}(t) = \langle t^2, e^t, \ln\sqrt{t}\rangle\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh bhi classification ka sawal hai: output angle brackets mein teen cheezon ke saath likha hai.
Yeh ordered triple hai, yani 11.3.1 ke mutabiq 3D vector-valued function ki shakal.
Rule: jab output ke kai components hon to function vector-valued hota hai.
Plan: components pehchanein, ek \(t\) par value nikalein, aur domain batayein.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\mathbf{h}(t) = \langle t^2, e^t, \ln\sqrt{t}\rangle\).
Maloom karna: yeh scalar hai ya vector-valued, aur kyun?
Tareeqa: 11.3.1 ke criteria: scalar function ka output ek akela number hota hai; vector-valued function ka output ordered tuple (components, ya \(\hat{i}, \hat{j}, \hat{k}\) ka combination) hota hai. \(t\) ki ek value rakh kar output dekhein.

Components pehchanein
\[\mathbf{h}(t) = t^2\,\hat{i} + e^t\,\hat{j} + \ln\sqrt{t}\,\hat{k}\]
Kyun: ordered triple \(\langle h_1, h_2, h_3\rangle\) ka matlab vector \(h_1\hat{i} + h_2\hat{j} + h_3\hat{k}\) hai. Har component khud \(t\) ka scalar function hai: yahi 11.1.2 ki definition hai.
Teen components ka matlab: \(x\), \(y\) aur \(z\) teeno simton mein alag alag value.

\(t\) ki ek value rakhein
\[\mathbf{h}(1) = \langle 1, e, 0\rangle = \hat{i} + e\,\hat{j}\]
Kyun: output space mein ek vector hai (teen components), ek number nahin. Bold harf \(\mathbf{h}\) bhi vector functions wale criterion (ii) ke mutabiq hai.
Dhyan dein: teesra component \(\ln 1 = 0\) hai, magar zero component ho to bhi output vector hi rehta hai.

Tasdeeq: yeh kahan defined hai?
\(\ln\sqrt{t}\) ke liye \(t > 0\) chahiye; \(t^2\) aur \(e^t\) par koi pabandi nahin.
\[\text{Domain} = (0, \infty)\]
Kyun: har \(t > 0\) par output teen components wala vector hai \(\checkmark\).
Yaad rahe: domain ka sawal alag hai; vector ya scalar hone ka faisla output ki shakal karti hai.
blocks.final_answer: Vector-valued function (3D): har \(t > 0\) par teen components wala vector milta hai, misaal \(\mathbf{h}(1) = \langle 1, e, 0\rangle\).

blocks.prompt: 8 (iii) Determine whether the following function is a scalar function or a vector-valued function. Give appropriate reasoning to support the answer: \(g(t) = \tan(t) + \csc(t)\)
blocks.explanation:
Is classification ke sawal mein ek chaal hai: do terms "+" se jure hue hain.
Lekin \(\tan t\) aur \(\csc t\) dono numbers hain, aur do numbers ka jama phir ek hi number hota hai.
Rule: vector ke components \(\hat{i}, \hat{j}\) se alag rakhe jate hain; yahan aisa kuch nahin.
Plan: ek \(t\) par value nikalenge aur samjhayenge ke "+" se vector kyun nahin banta.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(g(t) = \tan t + \csc t\).
Maloom karna: yeh scalar hai ya vector-valued, aur kyun?
Tareeqa: 11.3.1 ke criteria: scalar function ka output ek akela number hota hai; vector-valued function ka output ordered tuple (components, ya \(\hat{i}, \hat{j}, \hat{k}\) ka combination) hota hai. \(t\) ki ek value rakh kar output dekhein.

\(t\) ki ek value rakhein
\[g\left(\tfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \tan\tfrac{\pi}{4} + \csc\tfrac{\pi}{4}\]
\[= 1 + \sqrt{2} \approx 2.414\]
Kyun: \(\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1\) aur \(\csc\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{1}{\sin(\pi/4)} = \sqrt{2}\). Do real numbers jama kiye to ek real number aaya, jaise 2 seb aur 3 seb mil kar 5 seb, do alag cheezein nahin rehte.

Criteria lagayein
Output ek akela number: haan; naam chhota harf \(g\). Koi unit vector \(\hat{i}, \hat{j}\) nahin jo dono terms ko alag components bana kar rakhe.
Kyun: \(f(t)\,\hat{i} + g(t)\,\hat{j}\) mein unit vectors hisson ko alag rakhte hain, is liye woh vector hai. \(\tan t + \csc t\) mein dono numbers bas jama ho jate hain.
Dhyan dein: sirf "+" dekh kar vector keh dena sab se aam ghalti hai.

Tasdeeq: yeh kahan defined hai?
\(\tan t\) ke liye \(t \ne \frac{\pi}{2} + n\pi\); \(\csc t\) ke liye \(t \ne n\pi\).
\[t \ne \tfrac{n\pi}{2},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\]
Kyun: har ijazat wali \(t\) par value ek hi real number hai \(\checkmark\).
Is liye \(g\) ka graph ek aam curve hai jo har ijazat wale \(t\) par ek hi height deta hai.
blocks.final_answer: Scalar function: do real numbers ka jama ek real number hai (misaal \(g(\frac{\pi}{4}) = 1 + \sqrt{2}\)).

blocks.prompt: 8 (iv) Determine whether the following function is a scalar function or a vector-valued function. Give appropriate reasoning to support the answer: \(\mathbf{j}(t) = \left\langle \frac{1}{t^2+1}, \frac{1}{t^2+1}\right\rangle\)
blocks.explanation:
Is classification ke sawal mein doosri chaal hai: dono components barabar hain.
Phir bhi output ordered pair hai, jo 2D vector-valued function ki shakal hai.
Rule: faisla output ke components ki ginti se hota hai, un ki values se nahin.
Plan: \(\hat{i}, \hat{j}\) ke saath likhenge, ek \(t\) par value nikalenge, aur domain batayenge.
Yaad rahe: ek number ho to scalar, ek se zyada components hon to vector.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\mathbf{j}(t) = \left\langle \frac{1}{t^2+1}, \frac{1}{t^2+1}\right\rangle\).
Maloom karna: yeh scalar hai ya vector-valued, aur kyun?
Tareeqa: 11.3.1 ke criteria: scalar function ka output ek akela number hota hai; vector-valued function ka output ordered tuple (components, ya \(\hat{i}, \hat{j}, \hat{k}\) ka combination) hota hai. \(t\) ki ek value rakh kar output dekhein.

Components pehchanein
\[\mathbf{j}(t) = \dfrac{1}{t^2+1}\,\hat{i} + \dfrac{1}{t^2+1}\,\hat{j}\]
Kyun: ordered pair \(\langle j_1, j_2\rangle\) ka matlab plane ka vector \(j_1\hat{i} + j_2\hat{j}\) hai.
Angle brackets \(\langle\ ,\ \rangle\) dekhte hi samajh jayein ke output mein components hain.

\(t\) ki values rakhein
\[\mathbf{j}(0) = \langle 1, 1\rangle = \hat{i} + \hat{j}\]
\[\mathbf{j}(1) = \left\langle \tfrac{1}{2}, \tfrac{1}{2}\right\rangle\]
Kyun: output ke do components hain aur direction bhi (line \(y = x\) ki simt mein). Components barabar hon to bhi woh ek number nahin bante; jaise kisi ko "1 km east aur 1 km north" jana ho to yeh do hidayat hain, ek nahin.
Dhyan dein: barabar components dekh kar scalar keh dena ghalat hai.

Tasdeeq: yeh kahan defined hai?
\[t^2 + 1 \ge 1 > 0\]
is liye denominator kabhi zero nahin; domain \(\mathbb{R}\) hai aur har output 2D vector hai \(\checkmark\).
Yaad rahe: \(\mathbf{j}(t)\) ka bold harf bhi batata hai ke yeh vector function hai (11.3.1 (ii)).
blocks.final_answer: Vector-valued function (2D): har \(t \in \mathbb{R}\) par ordered pair milta hai, misaal \(\mathbf{j}(0) = \langle 1, 1\rangle\); barabar components se yeh scalar nahin banta.
